commitResults.messageBody:
All task data input into Turtley.java's run are
forgotten after the run terminates.

The task data should be preserved across runs
so that Turtley.java can keep track of user's
tasks accurately in the long term.

Storing all task data into a text file will
help preserve the inputted task data.

Let's start implementing this (using codex) by
creating a Storage class that controls writing to
a text file. add, mark, unmark, and delete methods
in Turtley.java will write to the file after
every operation. Reading from file is not
implemented and a new text file is created each
run for now.

commitResults.messageBody:
The deadline and event tasks only displayed timing
without having any operations attached to them.

User should have access to their timing in a
more useful format that String.

store the datetime in a Temporal variable.

This will allow the datetime can be used for
future operations and classification.

Consolidate task loading and saving in Storage
commitResults.messageBody: Move the existing save-file loading implementation into Storage so one class owns both persistence directions. Update Turtley to load through Storage and remove the redundant StorageReader class. Preserve the current file format, validation, and user-visible behavior while reducing the number of persistence responsibilities spread across the codebase.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task collection into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList as the owner of Turtley's ordered tasks and basic collection operations, including capacity checks and a read-only view for persistence. Update Turtley to use the new abstraction for access, mutations, capacity checks, and saving. Keep command parsing, user-facing output, and existing task behavior unchanged so the refactoring remains incremental and low risk.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce Parser to translate raw user input into typed commands with trimmed arguments. Replace Turtley’s string and prefix checks with dispatch on the parsed command while preserving all existing command recognition, invalid-input behavior, and task-specific execution. Keep command execution and user-facing messages in Turtley for this incremental step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console interaction into Ui
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce Ui to own console input, separators, startup and shutdown messages, errors, task confirmations, list rendering, and timecheck display helpers. Update Turtley to delegate all user-facing interaction to Ui while retaining task operations and command execution. Preserve the existing command-line behavior and output so this remains a safe incremental refactoring step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce executable command hierarchy
commitResults.messageBody: Add an abstract Command contract with executable concrete commands for every supported input, including shared AddCommand and IndexedCommand bases. Update Parser to construct commands and simplify Turtley into a uniform read-parse-execute loop with centralized error handling and exit detection. Convert Storage to an instance-based persistence service and hydrate TaskList through its constructor so commands receive explicit application collaborators. Preserve the existing command-line behavior and persistence semantics while completing the stretch-goal architecture.
